questions.question: If 19 July 2000 was a Wednesday, then what would be the day of the week on 15 June 2012?
questions.questionHtml: If 19 July 2000 was a Wednesday, then what would be the day of the week on 15 June 2012?
questions.solution:
Odd days:

A non-leap year has 365 days and a leap year has 366 days.

Non-leap year = 365 days or 52 weeks and 1 day. So, here the number of odd days is 1.

Leap year = 366 days or 52 weeks and 2 days So, here the number of odd days are 2.

Leap year between 2000 to 2012 = 2004, 2008 and 2012

And,

The non-leap year between 2000 and 2012 = 2001, 2002, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011

So, total number of odd day between 2000 and 2012 = 9 (Total Non- leap year) + 2 + 2 + 2 = 15 days = 1 odd day

Code of the day

Day

Sunday

Monday

2

Tuesday

3

Wednesday

4

Thursday

19 July 2000 was a Wednesday

=> Day on 19 July 2012 = Wednesday + 15

= Wednesday + remainder of 15/7

= Wednesday + 1 (odd day) = Thursday

Therefore, 19 July 2012 = Thursday

Now,

15 June 2012 = 19 July 2012 – 34 days

= Thursday – 34

= Thursday – the remainder of 34/7

= Thursday – 6 (In reverse direction)

= Friday

Hence, 15 June 2012 was “Friday”.

questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule:

  

Given equation 14 * 7 * 39 * 133 * 19 * 130

Option 1: Using the combination ×, +, –, ÷, =

14 × 7 + 39 – 133 ÷ 19 = 130

By BODMAS rule

14 × 7 + 39 – 7 = 130

98 + 39 – 7 = 130

137 – 7 = 130

130 = 130 (LHS = RHS)

Option 2: Using combination ×, –, +, ÷, =

14 × 7 – 39 + 133 ÷ 19 = 130

14 × 7 – 39 + 7 = 130

98 – 39 + 7 = 130

105 – 39 = 130

66 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3: Using the combination ÷, +, –, ×, =

14 ÷ 7 + 39 – 133 ×19 = 130

2 + 39 – 133 ×19 = 130

2 + 39 – 2527 = 130

41 – 2527 = 130

– 2486 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4: Using the combination ÷, –, +, ×, =

14 ÷ 7 – 39 + 133 × 19 = 130

2 – 39 + 133 × 19 = 130

2 – 39 + 2527 = 130

2529 – 39 = 130

2529 – 39 = 130

2490 = 130 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is “×, +, –, ÷, =”.

questions.question: Who among the following issued Mahzarnama in 1579?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following issued Mahzarnama in 1579?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Akbar.

Key Points

  • Akbar issued a Declaration or Mahzar.
  • Mahzar means pronouncement, declaration, or an opinion. It also implies petition.
  • He removed the Chief Preacher at Fatehpur Sikri and himself mounted the Pulpit of Jama Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri on June 22, 1579, and read the Khutba in his own names as the prophet and caliphs.
  • The Khutba was composed in verse by Faizi.
  • Mahzar was issued in September 1579 and it was prepared by Sheikh Mubarak.
  • Mahzar was signed by all the prominent Muslim theologians and divines of the Mughal empire.
  • It was also signed by Makhdum-ul-Mulk and Abdun Nabi, although they were known to be bitter critics of Akbar's liberal religious policy.
  • As instituted under the Mahzar, it was decided that Akbar would have the right to be the supreme arbiter or interpreter of Islamic laws, and he could decide in the matter of differing opinions on all religious questions.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a part of Gondwanaland?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following was NOT a part of Gondwanaland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is North America.

Key Points

  • Gondwanaland:
    • It was an ancient supercontinent that broke up about 180 million years ago.
    • The Gondwana land included India, Australia, South Africa, and South America as one single landmass.
    • Gondwana became the largest piece of the continental crust of the Paleozoic.
    • Gondwana existed from the Neoproterozoic period, that is, around 550 million years ago.
    • During the Eocene period, the Drake passage was opened up separating Antarctica and South America.
    • The continent of Gondwana was named by the Austrian scientist Eduard Suess, after the Gondwana region of central India which is derived from Sanskrit for 'forest of the Gonds'.
    • As per the earlier definition, Gondwana was not considered a supercontinent, as the landmasses of Siberia, Laurentia, Baltica were separated from it.
    • During the Paleozoic era, the largest piece of continental crust was the Gondwana, it was about 1/5th of the earth's surface.
    • Gondwana merged with Euramerica, during the Carboniferous period, to form the larger supercontinent called Pangea.
    • However, during the Mesozoic era, Pangea and Gondwana broke up.
    • Two-thirds of today's continental area is made up of Gondwana which includes the Indian subcontinent, Australia, Antarctica, Arabia, Zealandia, Africa, and South America.

  • When there is a disruption in this metabolism, there is an increase in the amount of bilirubin in the blood which leads to jaundice.
  • Jaundice is not a disease in itself but a sign of some other underlying problem.

    • Radar and Active Array Battery Multifunction Radar - with one launcher.
    • Both radars have 360-degree coverage with the search on move and track on move capabilities.
    • The system is compact, uses a single-stage solid propelled missile, and has a mid-course inertial navigation system with a two-way data link and terminal active seeker developed indigenously by DRDO.

Given:

Concept used:

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

(a - b)2 = a2 + b2 - 2ab

Calculation:

9(a2 + b2) + c2 + 20 = 12(a + 2b)

⇒ 40x2 - 200x + 180x - 900 = 40x2 + 200x - 216x - 1080

questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The mouse, however, reached his hole in safety.

B. A bull was bitten by a mouse, and, pained by the wound, tried to capture him.

C. The mouse, peeping out, crept up his flank and, again biting him, retreated to his hole.

D. The bull dug into the walls with his horns until wearied, he crouched down and slept by the hole.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "a bull bitten by a mouse". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
  • Sentence A will come after B as it is telling that the mouse reached safely in his hole after biting the bull.
  • Sentence D will come after A as it is explaining what the bull had done to catch the mouse.
  • The sentence 'C' is the concluding part because it is telling how the mouse again succeded in biting the bull.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: A bull was bitten by a mouse, and, pained by the wound, tried to capture him. The mouse, however, reached his hole in safety. The bull dug into the walls with his horns until wearied, he crouched down and slept by the hole. The mouse, peeping out, crept up his flank and, again biting him, retreated to his hole.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question: Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is essential for the marketer to study the behavior of the consumers in order to make better strategic marketing decisions. B. The study of consumer behavior is equally important for non-profit organizations such as governmental agencies, hospitals, NGOs, charitable organizations. C. Thus, studying consumer behavior before and during purchase helps in production scheduling, designing, pricing, positioning, segmentation, advertising and other promotional activities. D. If the marketer has complete knowledge about the consumer’s likings or disliking, then he can predict the response of the potential customers towards his offerings.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is essential for the marketer to study the behavior of the consumers in order to make better strategic marketing decisions.

B. The study of consumer behavior is equally important for non-profit organizations such as governmental agencies, hospitals, NGOs, charitable organizations.

C. Thus, studying consumer behavior before and during purchase helps in production scheduling, designing, pricing, positioning, segmentation, advertising and other promotional activities.

D. If the marketer has complete knowledge about the consumer’s likings or disliking, then he can predict the response of the potential customers towards his offerings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ADCB.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "studying the behavior of the consumers by the marketer". Hence, 'A' is the first part.
  • Sentence D will come after A as it is explaining how the marketer can predict the response of the potential customers.
  • Sentence C will come after D as it is explaining how the customer behavior study helps the marketer.
  • The sentence 'B' is the concluding part because it is telling how the study of consumer behavior helps other non-profit organizations as well.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: It is essential for the marketer to study the behavior of the consumers in order to make better strategic marketing decisions. If the marketer has complete knowledge about the consumer’s likings or disliking, then he can predict the response of the potential customers towards his offerings. Thus, studying consumer behavior before and during purchase helps in production scheduling, designing, pricing, positioning, segmentation, advertising, and other promotional activities. The study of consumer behavior is equally important for non-profit organizations such as governmental agencies, hospitals, NGOs, charitable organizations.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
       

Hinglish

  • वाक्य 'A' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "बाज़ारिया द्वारा उपभोक्ताओं के व्यवहार का अध्ययन" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः 'A' पहला भाग है।

  • वाक्य C, D के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह समझा रहा है कि ग्राहक व्यवहार अध्ययन कैसे बाज़ारिया की मदद करता है।

Key Points

  • The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
    • The commas, inverted commas are removed, and 'if' is added in place of the question mark (?) as the yes/no type of question is reported by using 'asked' + 'if/whether' + clause.
    • The second-person pronoun ''you'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''he''.
    • The present perfect tense format 'Subject + have + V3 (heard) + Object' will be changed into the past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (heard) + Object'.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Additional Information

  • We use 'less' in comparative structures, especially before uncountable nouns.
  • 'Less' is used to express inadequacy or insufficiency of something, but only in a comparative sense.
    • Example: I have less homework to do today than I had yesterday.
  • 'Little' indicates a small size, amount, or degree of something you cannot count.
  • 'Little' refers to non-countable nouns and is used with the singular form.
    • Example: I have little homework to do before I leave.
  • Therefore, the adjective 'little' should be used in place of the adjective 'less'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: Sameer gave very little information to Muneer about the progress of the work.

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खण्ड में adjective 'less' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • 'Less' किसी ऐसी चीज़ की छोटी मात्रा को इंगित करता है जिसे आप गिन नहीं सकते और जिसकी आप तुलना कर रहे हैं।

  • 'Little' non-countable nouns को संदर्भित करता है और एकवचन रूप के साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है।
    • उदाहरण: I have little homework to do before I leave.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'An impressive parade was put up by the armed forces on Republic Day.'

Key Points

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the past simple tense.
  • When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject ''The armed forces'' of the active voice becomes the object, the object ''an impressive parade'' becomes the subject.
  • The active format "V2 (put)" should be converted into the passive format "was + V3 (put)".
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Additional Information

Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
 

 

Hinglish

  • Active Voice में , एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है।
  • Passive Voice में , एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य active voice में है और यह past simple tense में है।
  • जब हम इस वाक्य को passive voice में बदलते हैं, तो active voice का subject 'The armed forces', object बन जाता है और object 'an impressive parade', subject बन जाता है।
  • Active format "V2 (put)" को passive format "was + V3 (put)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए।
  • यह past simple tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है।
     

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।
